skill.name: when-optimizing-agent-learning-use-reasoningbank-intelligence
skill.description: Build adaptive agent learning workflows with ReasoningBank, trajectory tracking, pattern extraction, model training, and performance validation.
skill.summary: Create a structured ReasoningBank workflow for learning from agent trajectories and improving future strategy choices.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are markdown fences or JavaScript template literals and were false positives. I confirmed one documented npx workflow command and the fixed /tmp export examples as medium risks. I also found a high-severity data-handling issue because trajectories and exports can contain sensitive agent reasoning without redaction.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a vetted version, document package provenance, and require explicit user confirmation before running workflow commands.
Write exports to a user-selected project directory, create files with restricted permissions, and avoid fixed names under /tmp.
Redact secrets and private prompts before storage, limit exported fields, and document retention and access-control requirements.

content.value_statement: Agents often repeat weak strategies because learning data stays unstructured. This skill organizes trajectories, patterns, benchmarks, and recommendations into a ReasoningBank workflow.
actual_capabilities: Defines a five-phase workflow for initializing ReasoningBank, capturing trajectories, optimizing strategies, validating gains, and exporting outputs.
Shows JavaScript examples for trajectory schemas, verdict scoring, pattern extraction, recommendation generation, benchmarking, and reporting.
Includes optional AgentDB guidance for HNSW indexing, quantization, and vector similarity search.
Specifies validation criteria, success metrics, output artifacts, and deployment readiness checks.
Provides hook examples for claude-flow pre-task and post-task memory integration.
limitations: Examples are illustrative and require real ReasoningBank, agent, and memory implementations.
It does not include a complete runnable package or automated tests.
Model quality depends on diverse trajectories and reliable success metrics.
The export examples use local temporary files and should be hardened before production.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Strategy Selection
use_cases.description: Capture successful and failed trajectories, then turn repeated patterns into prioritized strategy recommendations.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Learning Gains
use_cases.description: Compare baseline and optimized agents with shared test cases and clear performance metrics.

use_cases.title: Prepare Learning Artifacts for Deployment
use_cases.description: Package models, pattern libraries, integration notes, and learning reports for controlled production rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Learning Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new agent learning project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a ReasoningBank setup for my agent. Include required storage, trajectory fields, verdict criteria, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Useful Trajectories
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate guidance for collecting training data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a trajectory capture plan for my agent. Include success signals, failure labels, privacy safeguards, and pattern extraction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Existing Agents
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for improving current agent behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze my current agent workflow and propose ReasoningBank optimizations, benchmark tests, and recommendation ranking criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Learning System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a production rollout plan for learned strategies. Include export controls, monitoring, retraining cadence, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: I need my support agent to learn from repeated ticket resolutions.
output: A trajectory schema covering ticket context, decision steps, actions, observations, and outcome metrics.
Verdict criteria for speed, accuracy, customer satisfaction, and escalation avoidance.
A validation plan comparing baseline and optimized resolution performance.

output_examples.input: I want to know which learned strategies should be applied first.
output: A ranked recommendation list based on frequency, average score, consistency, and applicable contexts.
A short explanation of why each strategy is safe to test.
Benchmark checks that confirm improvement before production rollout.

output_examples.input: I need a deployment checklist for a trained decision model.
output: Export readiness checks for model weights, patterns, recommendations, and performance evidence.
Security checks for redaction, file permissions, and approved storage locations.
Monitoring steps for drift, success rate changes, and scheduled retraining.

best_practices: Collect both successful and failed trajectories before training recommendations.
Define measurable verdict criteria before comparing baseline and optimized agents.
Redact private data before storing trajectories, reports, or exported learning artifacts.
anti_patterns: Do not train from only successful examples because recommendations will be biased.
Do not deploy learned strategies before benchmark results show stable improvement.
Do not store reasoning traces or reports in shared locations without access controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build a workflow for adaptive agent learning with trajectory capture, pattern extraction, model training, and validation.

faq.question: Does it include a complete runnable application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that require real project code and dependencies.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is tool-agnostic and the marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.

faq.question: What data should be collected?
faq.answer: Collect task context, reasoning steps, actions, observations, outcomes, and metrics that are safe to retain.

faq.question: How should teams validate improvement?
faq.answer: Run baseline and optimized agents on shared test cases, then compare score, success rate, efficiency, and quality.

faq.question: What security precautions are important?
faq.answer: Pin external packages, avoid fixed temporary paths, redact sensitive traces, and restrict access to exported artifacts.
